a: Precision = TP/(TP+FP): of everything I flagged, how much was right — punish false alarms. Recall (sensitivity) = TP/(TP+FN): of everything real, how much did I catch — punish misses. Specificity = TN/(TN+FP): how well I recognized negatives. F1 is the harmonic mean of precision and recall — it punishes imbalance between them, so a model with 100% precision but 5% recall scores near 0.09, not a 'pass'. Which to prioritize is a business decision: cancer screening wants recall, spam filter wants precision.

Transformers were introduced because RNNs process tokens sequentially, blocking parallelism and forgetting long-range context; attention processes everything at once with direct token-to-token links. Query, Key, Value are three different projections of each token's embedding: the query is 'what am I looking for', the key is 'what I contain', the value is 'what I will hand over'. Three separate projections (not one) let a token seek one kind of information while offering another — like a search engine where page titles (keys), your query, and page content (values) differ. Scores = query dot key (scaled by 1/sqrt(d)), softmaxed into weights over values.

Assumption violations show up in residuals: heteroscedasticity — error variance changes with the fitted value (funnel shape); fixes: log-transform the target, weighted least squares, or robust standard errors (predictions stay unbiased, but naive standard errors are wrong). Autocorrelation — residuals correlate with each other, common in time data (Durbin-Watson ~2 is clean, near 0 or 4 signals trouble); fixes: add lag features or switch to time-series models. Non-normal residuals mainly hurt confidence intervals and p-values; with large n the CLT softens it, otherwise transform the target or use bootstrap inference.

The determinant measures how a matrix scales area/volume — zero means the matrix collapses space, so it has no inverse (singular). The inverse 'undoes' the transformation (A times A-inverse = I) and solves A x = b directly — but numerically we prefer decomposition methods, and in ML explicitly inverting is usually avoided (ill-conditioned matrices). Rank is the number of independent rows/columns — the dimension of space the matrix can reach; full-rank design matrices are what make regression solvable, and rank deficiency is exactly multicollinearity.

Subword algorithms build vocabularies between words and characters: BPE starts from characters and merges the most frequent pair iteratively; WordPiece (BERT) merges the pair that maximizes likelihood, marking continuation pieces with ##; SentencePiece (used by LLaMA/T5) treats text as raw bytes/characters with no pre-tokenization — language-agnostic and even reversible (no unknown tokens). Vocabulary size (30k-100k) trades model size against sequence length: smaller vocab = longer token sequences = more compute per sentence.

kw: employees earning more than their manager
a: Self-join compares rows within one table via aliases: SELECT e.name FROM emp e JOIN emp m ON e.manager_id = m.id WHERE e.salary > m.salary. The trick generalizes to many interview classics: finding duplicates (match on the key, different id), consecutive-day logins (join on date + 1), and pairwise comparisons. Beware duplicates from one-to-many matches — DISTINCT or window functions tidy the output.

Top-N per group is a window-function signature: SELECT * FROM (SELECT *, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY dept ORDER BY salary DESC) rk FROM emp) t WHERE rk <= 3 — DENSE_RANK so tied salaries all make the cut. 'Customers who ordered every month' is relational division: count distinct months per customer in the period and compare with the total months (SELECT customer_id FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT MONTH(order_date)) = 12). Both patterns appear constantly in interviews because they test aggregation plus window thinking.

Imbalance toolbox beyond SMOTE: undersampling the majority (random, or informed like Tomek links removing ambiguous boundary pairs) — fast but discards data; oversampling the minority (random duplication, ADASYN focusing on hard examples); class weights or focal loss make the model pay asymmetric costs without touching data; ensemble resampling trains one model per balanced subset and votes. Evaluation must stratify: PR-AUC over ROC-AUC when positives are rare, plus per-class recall and a confusion matrix on an untouched test set.

Point fixes: at/iat are scalar-fast label/position accessors; transform ('apply but same-shape') builds group-level features without merge gymnastics; pipe chains functions in a readable pipeline; explode turns list-valued cells into rows; cut bins by value ranges while qcut bins by rank (quantiles); the .dt accessor extracts year/month/weekday vectorized. Together with .str methods these cover most 'how would you' pandas interview scenarios without a single Python loop.

Pretraining objectives: causal LM (GPT) predicts the next token left-to-right — generation-ready; masked LM (BERT) fills gaps using both directions — understanding-strong. Scaling laws (Chinchilla) showed loss falls predictably with compute, data, and parameters — and that many models were undertrained on data. 'Emergent abilities' are behaviors (multi-step reasoning, instruction following) that appear only at scale. In-context learning — solving tasks from examples in the prompt — is the strangest emergent one: no weight updates, yet the model 'learns' within the context window.

RAG details that decide quality: parsing — PDFs need layout-aware parsing (tables, columns); poor parsing poisons everything downstream. Query rewriting — LLM rewrites user queries into retrieval-friendly forms (HyDE writes a hypothetical answer and searches with it; multi-query fires several rewrites and fuses results). Parent-document retrieval embeds small chunks for precision but returns their full parent section for context. Context window stuffing fails quietly — order retrieved chunks by relevance, most important first and last.

Norms measure vector length: L2 (Euclidean — straight-line distance, sensitive to outliers), L1 (Manhattan — sum of absolute differences, robust, drives Lasso), Linf (max component). Cosine similarity measures the angle between vectors ignoring length — the standard for embedding similarity because meaning lives in direction, not magnitude. Euclidean suits dense low-dim spaces; cosine dominates text retrieval; and in high dimensions all pairwise distances concentrate, which is why ANN indexes use approximate methods.

Practical SQL patterns: upsert — INSERT ... ON CONFLICT/ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE or MERGE (update if exists else insert) — the standard idempotent load. DELETE with a join or subquery removes orphans (DELETE FROM orders WHERE customer_id NOT IN (SELECT id FROM customers) — prefer NOT EXISTS for NULL safety). WHERE vs HAVING performance: filter early — WHERE reduces rows before grouping, HAVING only filters aggregates after, so push conditions to WHERE whenever logically possible.

Classic NLP tasks: NER tags entities (person, org, date) — rule-based gazetteers, statistical CRFs, and now transformer token-classification heads; POS tagging labels grammatical roles feeding parsers; lemmatization maps inflected forms to dictionary form using context (better than stemming for search); text classification (sentiment, topic, intent) is the most common production NLP workload — start with TF-IDF + linear model as baseline, move to a fine-tuned encoder (DistilBERT) when accuracy matters, and to LLM prompting when labels are scarce.
